scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A flat panel sits in the sun, and runs fans and lights. No moving parts, no fuel. How?

scenes.name: silicon
scenes.text: Each panel is made of cells of silicon, the same material used in computer chips, built in two layers, called n type and p type.

scenes.name: field
scenes.text: Where the two layers meet, a junction forms, with a built in electric field.

scenes.name: photon
scenes.text: Sunlight arrives as tiny packets of energy, called photons. A photon knocks an electron loose from a silicon atom.

scenes.name: current
scenes.text: The field pushes the freed electrons one way, toward metal contacts. Connect a wire, and you get a direct current.

scenes.name: inverter
scenes.text: Homes run on alternating current, so an inverter converts it. Extra power can charge batteries, or go to the grid.

scenes.name: eff
scenes.text: Typical panels turn about twenty percent of sunlight into electricity. Most of the rest becomes heat.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Photon, electron, field, current. Sunlight, turned into power. Follow for more on how things really work.
